result_text:
I implemented all five requirements (BMS-001 to BMS-005) and wrote the tests, but I haven't run them. Bash was denied in this session, so `python3 -m pytest` never ran. Please run it before relying on the code.

- **`src/battery/bms.py`**:
  - `cell_fault` returns true if any cell is above 4.20 V or below 3.00 V (BMS-001/002).
  - `charge_permitted` returns true for 0–45 °C inclusive (BMS-003).
  - `BatteryController.step` latches `FAULT` on a cell fault. Otherwise it returns `CHARGING` when the charger is connected and charging is permitted, and `IDLE` if not (BMS-004).
  - `BatteryController.reset` moves `FAULT` to `IDLE` only when the cells passed in are healthy (BMS-005).
  - Each function and the class has the `# implements:` marker above it, per CONTRIBUTING.md. I added no helpers and left the public names and signatures unchanged.
- **`tests/test_bms.py`**: Each test carries `@pytest.mark.verifies(...)`. Together they cover every acceptance criterion, including both sides of each boundary: 4.20/4.21 V, 3.00/2.99 V and −0.1/0/45/45.1 °C. They also check the latch (healthy cells on the next step still give `FAULT`) and both reset cases.

I read "unless faulted" in BMS-004 as meaning only a cell fault puts the controller in `FAULT`. An over-temperature reading just gives `IDLE`, which matches the 50 °C acceptance case.

I didn't add anything to `FINDINGS.json`.
